forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: the weekend is a two-act story and act two is the big one. Right now (Sat dawn) there's a solid SSE groundswell on the coast — 6.1ft @ 9s from 166°, 599 kJ of energy — with light WSW offshore under it (11 kph gusting 17). That 166° is 14 degrees east of dead south, and those 14 degrees matter: Dee Why is the only one of the four rating FAIR-TO-GOOD this morning while Long Reef, Curl Curl and North Steyne all sit at FAIR. Nine seconds is short for that much water, so it's punchy and fast rather than lined-up. The 9:57am high is your friend — it takes the sting off the shallow banks. Wind stays offshore and light until roughly 2pm, then a light ENE sea breeze. Sunday is the upgrade: a genuine 13-second SE groundswell (146–150°) fills in overnight and doubles up with the existing swell — Long Reef jumps to 8–10ft (double overhead) by 9am, Dee Why to 4–6ft, and energy spikes past 1000 kJ by midday. But the Sunday wind window is short: NW offshore at dawn, swinging NE onshore by noon. Dawn to 10am Sunday, no later. Water 18.1°C (SharkSmart station median, 53 stations) — 3/2 steamer weather, air only ~11°C at first light. ✈️ Reminder: you're in Oahu until 13 Aug, so this whole weekend runs without you — use /hawaii-surf over there. 🦈 SharkSmart NSW read clean: no detections Palm Beach → Manly in the last 36h. ⚠️ Note: Surfline's regional forecaster commentary endpoint returned HTTP 500 this run, so this note is composed from the live Surfline point data (wave / wind / tide / rating / weather JSON), not quoted from a Surfline forecaster. Consistency figures were not exposed by the API this run.

wind.summary: Light WSW offshore through the whole morning — 11 kph gusting 17 at 9am, easing to about 7 kph SSW by midday. A light ENE sea breeze only arrives around 2–3pm, so this is a rare all-morning clean window rather than a dawn-only one.

shark.summary: No shark detections logged anywhere between Palm Beach and Manly in the last 36 hours. SMART drumline (349 features), DPI/SLS drone (82), Surf Life Saving NSW (144), trauma (7) and events (1) feeds all read clean this refresh.

days.label: Today
days.note: The best all-morning wind window in a fortnight — WSW offshore holds light right through to about 2pm instead of folding at 10am. Swell is 6.1ft @ 9s from 166° SSE (599 kJ), with enough east in it that Dee Why is the only spot rating fair-to-good while the rest sit fair. Short period means punchy and fast, not lined-up. Your 10am–12pm slot lands right on the 9:57am high, which softens the banks — go then, not later.

swells.label: The engine — SSE at 166°, far enough east of dead south that the Point and the open banks both get fed
Light ESE windswell filling in from midday — adds texture, not size

dee-why.window: 9am–12pm is the pick, and it's the only spot of the four rating fair-to-good. The 9:57am high fattens the inside just enough that a 9-second swell doesn't square up on the sandbank. WSW offshore holds until roughly 2pm. After the high drains, favour the Point over the open beach.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Frontside at the Point and for once the swell direction is on your side — 166° is the angle that actually wraps in rather than getting eaten by the headland. Nine seconds carries push but not much wall, so don't over-commit to the bottom turn: get up to speed off the take-off and put the first turn in the pocket while the section is still standing. 599 kJ at only 4–5ft means it hits harder than it looks.

swells.label: The engine — SSE at 166°, and the Reef takes it full in the chest
Light ESE windswell filling in from midday

long-reef.window: Biggest of the four, as always on a southerly. 6–9am has the most size (668 kJ at 6am, easing to 357 by noon) and the offshore is straightest early. Rates fair rather than fair-to-good because 9 seconds on that much size gets thick and lumpy.
alerts: 5–7ft on a 9-second period is a lot of water moving fast — short-interval swell of that size closes out sections that a 13-second swell would hold open. Pick your channel before you paddle out.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: The Reef corner is your frontside. On a short-period SSE the take-off zone shifts north of where it sits on a long-period south — sit wider and further up the point than instinct says. Step up on volume so you can make the drop early; you can't stall your way into these.

swells.label: The engine — SSE at 166°, straight into the open Curl Curl banks
Light ESE windswell filling in from midday

curl-curl.window: The size-to-risk sweet spot again — real punch without Long Reef's consequence. Mid-morning on the rise into the 9:57am high is the cleanest read; the North Curl Curl corner shelters best if the wind swings early.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Curl Curl's lefts are your backhand and 4–6ft on a punchy SSE is exactly their band. Short period means the wall runs away from you — keep weight forward off the drop and set the rail early rather than pumping down the line. If it's closing out, drift 100m south where the bank is deeper.

swells.label: The engine — SSE at 166°, but North Steyne sits deepest in the shadow
Light ESE windswell filling in from midday

manly.window: Half the size of Long Reef, as usual on a southerly. Clean and manageable all morning under the WSW offshore. The call only if you want a fun one rather than a serious one — or if the northern banks look too thick.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: Backhand on the North Steyne lefts. At waist-to-chest with 599 kJ behind it the wave still has more push than the size suggests — it'll surprise you off the take-off. Ride volume; this is not a step-up day down here.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The real swell of the weekend. A 13-second SE groundswell (146–150°) fills in overnight and doubles up with today's leftover — Long Reef jumps to 8–10ft by 9am and energy spikes past 1000 kJ around midday. But the wind window is short and hard: NW offshore at dawn (4–6 kts), swinging NE onshore by noon and 9 kts by 3pm. Dawn to 10am or don't bother. Tides: low 4:27am, high 10:35am, low 4:21pm, high 10:33pm.

dee-why.window: Best balance of the four on Sunday — 13 seconds at 146° is a long-period SE, the angle that actually wraps into the Point properly. First light to 10am under the NW offshore. The 10:35am high arrives right as the wind turns.
alerts: Wind flips NE onshore by noon — the Sunday window is genuinely dawn-to-10am, not dawn-to-lunch.

long-reef.window: Biggest surf of the weekend by a distance — double overhead at 9am on a 13-second SE, with energy climbing through the morning to 1015 kJ at midday. First light only; the NW offshore is gone by noon.
alerts: 8–10ft double-overhead on a genuine long-period groundswell. This is a step-up, know-your-channel, go-with-someone day — not a casual paddle.
Energy climbs through the morning (485 → 1015 kJ by midday) — it gets heavier as the wind gets worse. Go early.

curl-curl.window: The sensible version of Sunday — proper long-period size with a fraction of Long Reef's consequence. Thirteen seconds gives you a real wall instead of Saturday's short-interval chop. Dawn to 10am.
alerts: Wind flips NE onshore by noon — first three hours of light only.

manly.window: Finally gets a share of it — the extra east in a 146° swell reaches North Steyne where a dead-south never does. Chest to overhead early, clean under the NW. The manageable Sunday option.
alerts: Wind flips NE onshore by noon.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two very different days. Saturday is the friendlier one — moderate 9-second SSE, 4–7ft depending on spot, and an unusually long offshore window that holds to about 2pm. Sunday is the serious one — a 13-second SE groundswell doubling up to 8–10ft at Long Reef with over 1000 kJ behind it, but only a dawn-to-10am wind window before the NE onshore. If you want one good session, take Saturday mid-morning. If you want the wave of the weekend, take Sunday at first light and accept the size. Monday drops away hard (2–4ft) as the swell fades.

dee-why.window: Rates fair-to-good both days and it's the pick of the four for quality-to-risk. Saturday mid-morning on the high, or Sunday at first light when the 13-second SE finally gives the Point something to bend.

long-reef.window: Size leader both days, and Sunday it's in another league — 8–10ft on a long-period SE. Saturday early is the approachable version at 5–7ft.
alerts: Sunday reaches double overhead with 1000+ kJ behind it. Step-up equipment, first light, and a plan for getting back out.

curl-curl.window: The consistent middle across both days — 4–6ft Saturday, 5–7ft Sunday, always with less consequence than the Reef. North Curl Curl corner both mornings.

manly.window: Doubles in size from Saturday to Sunday as the swell swings east — 3–4ft Sat, 4–6ft Sun. Always the manageable option of the four.
